A feature is PASS only when it is implemented, persisted, reachable in the UI, tested, and the test is meaningful. Generated by inspection of the working tree, not from earlier reports.

features.name: Model-specific prompt compilation
features.implementation: film/prompt_compiler.py (ShotBrief: the 14-section common representation; targets declaring style/budget/negative/audio/motion with the basis of each convention; compile_prompt as a pure function), film/prompt_brief.py (briefs from a storyboard shot and from an analysed shot), film/shot_vocabulary.py (phrase tables shared with the host's own synthesis), handlers/prompt_handler.py, _routes/prompts.py

features.test: tests/test_prompt_compiler.py — 25 tests: target resolution incl. the unrecognised case, genuinely different output per family, action surviving into every target, scene intent never sent and never falsely reported as dropped, each drop-with-reason path, budget sacrifice order, continuity surviving truncation, both brief builders against the real app, the routes incl. the ambiguous-source 400, and model_specific actually filled

features.evidence: One brief compiled for five models produced five different strings: LTX prose, Wan labelled clauses, SDXL tags, FLUX with motion/timeline/negative dropped and each reported, and an unknown id marked matched=false. A request naming no source is refused with 400 rather than guessed at.

final_status_reason: Three product-critical capabilities from the brief are not implemented: AI timeline editing, the cross-project shot library, and per-version deletion. The PF2 knowledge engine and the model-specific prompt compiler now ship complete (implementation, persistence, UI, tests, e2e).
